chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Isma'il ibn Hammam said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: "The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) entered the Ka'bah and prayed in its four corners, two rak'ahs in each corner."

key_terms.الْكَعْبَة: The Ka'bah, the cubic building in Mecca
key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَ آلِهِ: Peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet pray inside the Ka'bah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of the Prophet’s specific prayer pattern within the Ka'bah, offering a foundational juristic basis for the permissibility (juz') and recommended status (mustahabb) of entering the sanctuary for worship. The detail of praying two rak'ahs in each corner highlights the Ka'bah not merely as a directional marker (qiblah) but as a distinct locus of devotion, a view supported by Shia jurists who cite this event to validate the ritual purity and sanctity of the interior space.
